title: Testicular torsion: testicular (gonadal) artery arises from the abdominal aorta
vignette: A 21-year-old previously healthy man comes to the emergency department with acute onset of severe left scrotal pain and nausea. The pain started after he returned home from the gym following an intense workout. He denies any trauma, fever, or dysuria. Examination shows a swollen and tender left testis that lies higher than the right testis. Doppler ultrasound shows decreased arterial blood flow in the left spermatic cord entering the testis. Which of the following is the likely origin of the artery involved in this patient's condition?

clues.text: acute onset of severe left scrotal pain and nausea
clues.note: Sudden severe scrotal pain with nausea/vomiting is the classic presentation of testicular torsion - a urologic emergency.

clues.text: lies higher than the right testis
clues.note: A high-riding testis (with possible horizontal lie/absent cremasteric reflex) is characteristic of torsion from twisting of the spermatic cord.

clues.text: decreased arterial blood flow in the left spermatic cord entering the testis
clues.note: Reduced arterial flow on Doppler confirms compromise of the TESTICULAR (gonadal) artery within the twisted spermatic cord.

whatMatters: Testicular torsion twists the spermatic cord, compromising the TESTICULAR (gonadal) ARTERY that supplies the testis. The gonadal arteries arise directly from the ABDOMINAL AORTA (just below the renal arteries). Answer A.
strategy: Identify the affected vessel (testicular/gonadal artery in the spermatic cord) and recall its origin: the gonadal arteries branch directly off the abdominal aorta (retroperitoneal, ~L2, below the renal arteries). Reject the iliac branches and others: external iliac (-> femoral, lower limb), internal iliac (pelvic viscera), internal pudendal (perineum/scrotal SKIN, not the testis), obturator (medial thigh), and renal artery (kidney; its branches don't supply the testis).

eliminations.label: External iliac artery - becomes femoral (lower limb)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the external iliac artery passes under the inguinal ligament to become the femoral artery. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies the lower extremity, not the testis. ✅ Correct if: lower-limb arterial supply.

eliminations.label: Internal iliac artery - pelvic viscera
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the internal iliac supplies the pelvic wall/viscera, buttock, and medial thigh. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: the testis is supplied by the gonadal artery from the aorta, not the internal iliac. ✅ Correct if: bladder/rectum/pelvic organ supply.

eliminations.label: Internal pudendal artery - scrotal SKIN, not testis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a branch of the internal iliac supplying the perineum, anal canal, and external genital SKIN (scrotum/penis). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it supplies scrotal skin, not the testis itself (which the gonadal artery supplies). ✅ Correct if: perineal/external genital skin blood supply.

eliminations.label: Obturator artery - medial thigh
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a branch of the internal iliac supplying the medial thigh/pelvis. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it does not supply the testis. ✅ Correct if: medial thigh/hip supply.

eliminations.label: Renal artery - kidney (branches don't reach the testis)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: supplies the kidney (and ureteric branches). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: although the gonadal artery arises NEAR the renal arteries, it comes off the AORTA directly, not from the renal artery, and the renal artery doesn't supply the testis. ✅ Correct if: renal/ureteric blood supply.

reasoning: Acute severe scrotal pain + high-riding testis + decreased Doppler flow = testicular torsion
Torsion twists the spermatic cord, compromising the testicular (gonadal) artery
The gonadal arteries branch directly off the abdominal aorta (below the renal arteries)
mechanism: Testicular torsion results from twisting of the spermatic cord (often from inadequate fixation of the testis to the tunica vaginalis - a 'bell-clapper' deformity), which compresses first the venous (pampiniform plexus) and then the arterial supply, threatening hemorrhagic infarction; it presents with acute severe scrotal pain, nausea/vomiting, a high-riding/horizontal testis, and an absent cremasteric reflex, and is a surgical emergency (detorsion/orchiopexy within ~6 hours). The testis is supplied by the TESTICULAR (GONADAL) ARTERY, which travels in the spermatic cord and arises directly from the ABDOMINAL AORTA at about L2, just BELOW the renal arteries (the gonadal arteries descend retroperitoneally, cross the ureter and external iliac vessels, and traverse the inguinal canal). Note the venous drainage differs: the right gonadal VEIN drains into the inferior vena cava, whereas the left gonadal vein drains into the LEFT RENAL vein. The distractor arteries supply other regions - external iliac (lower limb), internal iliac and its branches (pelvic viscera, perineum/scrotal skin via internal pudendal, medial thigh via obturator) - and the renal artery supplies the kidney, not the testis.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Anatomy > gonadal (testicular/ovarian) arteries arise from the abdominal aorta (~L2, below renal arteries); testicular torsion compromises the testicular artery in the spermatic cord; right gonadal vein -> IVC, left -> left renal vein.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Torsion compromises the testicular (gonadal) artery, which branches off the abdominal aorta.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on testicular torsion, gonadal/testicular artery, spermatic cord, cremasteric reflex, or bell-clapper deformity? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Internal pudendal supplies scrotal SKIN (not testis); iliac branches supply limb/pelvis; renal artery supplies kidney - the testis is fed from the aorta.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: testicular (gonadal) artery from abdominal aorta (~L2); torsion = surgical emergency; left gonadal vein -> left renal vein.

keywords.front: Acute scrotal pain + high-riding testis + ↓Doppler flow

keywords.back: Perineum + external genital SKIN (scrotum/penis), not the testis

keywords.front: Right vs left gonadal VEIN drainage
keywords.back: Right -> IVC; left -> left renal vein

firstAid.detail: Anatomy: testicular/ovarian arteries branch off the abdominal aorta (~L2).
Anatomy > internal pudendal (scrotal skin), iliac (limb/pelvis), renal (kidney).

memoryHook: The testis started high in the abdomen, so its artery comes straight off the aorta and rides down the cord; twist the cord (torsion) and that aortic branch gets choked off.
